evidence.detail: The repository HEAD exactly matches the launcher-bound target commit.
ROADMAP.md exists at the target commit and identifies itself as draft roadmap v4 awaiting this review and exact human approval.
The M2 roadmap defines five sequential work items, per-issue boundaries, verification, documentation, risks, and definitions of done.

The approved brief still specifies the named app-only security check as ending with secret discard after the outbound token request, despite DECISION-014 and roadmap v4 requiring session-lifetime retention and silent renewal.
ISSUE-0010 relies on static source assertions to verify several runtime browser behaviors, including clearing the secret after submission, mode changes, and logout.
The governance validator could not execute because the read-only review environment had no usable temporary directory; it failed before producing a validation result.

evidence: The approved brief requires the app-only security review to follow the lifecycle “UI field → POST body → memory → outbound token request → discard” at project/brief/PROJECT_BRIEF.md:246-250.
DECISION-014 requires retaining the secret for the app-only session and silently renewing tokens, and ROADMAP.md:131-145 and :174 adopt that model.

A milestone reviewer following the approved brief literally could require immediate discard, while one following the decision and roadmap could require retention and renewal. This makes the security acceptance target contradictory.
findings.remediation: Amend the brief's named security-check lifecycle to say the secret is retained in server memory for the app-only session, reused for silent renewal, and cleared on logout, supersession, and process exit, explicitly binding that clarification to DECISION-014. Keep the roadmap wording aligned.
findings.title: Approved brief contradicts the decided secret-retention lifecycle
findings.verification: Re-read the brief, DECISION-014, and roadmap and confirm all three specify the same retention, renewal, and clearing events with no remaining immediate-discard requirement.

evidence: ROADMAP.md:204 makes clearing the browser field after submit, mode switch, and logout an acceptance criterion but names only static assertions over committed web sources as its verification.

Static source inspection can confirm that clearing assignments exist, but cannot establish that the relevant event paths execute successfully or that the secret does not remain referenced in JavaScript state.
The verification strategy at ROADMAP.md:219-221 likewise describes UI coverage only as static-safety assertions.
findings.remediation: Add a concrete offline behavioral verification method for the app-only UI lifecycle, covering submit success and failure, mode switch, and logout. This may be a documented manual browser walkthrough with synthetic credentials and mocked/local responses if adding a JavaScript test toolchain would violate the zero-dependency constraint; record observable expected results and evidence.
findings.title: Runtime secret-clearing behavior is covered only by static assertions
findings.verification: Execute the specified offline behavioral check and record evidence that each relevant event clears the field and leaves no secret in application-controlled browser state, while retaining the existing static safety checks.

limitations: The governance validator could not run in the read-only environment because Python could not create a temporary directory. No validator pass is claimed.
No live Microsoft identity or Graph operation was performed; the roadmap correctly classifies those operations as separately approved protected actions and a residual evidence gap.

No standalone ISSUE-0007 through ISSUE-0011 records exist yet. project/issues/README.md says issue files are created for approved roadmap issues, so the detailed roadmap rows were treated as the proposed work items for this pre-approval review.
review.summary: The v4 roadmap is substantially detailed and sensibly sequenced, but it cannot pass until the approved brief and roadmap agree on the central secret-retention lifecycle and ISSUE-0010 has behavioral evidence for its runtime secret-clearing criteria. Target identity is valid. Governance validation was unavailable due the read-only environment's lack of a usable temporary directory.
